title: Enterprise onboarding, escalation, integration, and QBR playbook (Comprehensive)
author: Asha Banerjee
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference standard operating procedures for enterprise onboarding, escalation handling, integration guidance, known issues and workarounds, and QBR / health check materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Support, Solutions Engineering, and SRE partners who operate and scale enterprise accounts. Use this playbook during onboarding, routine health checks, escalations, and quarterly business reviews.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable, role-based onboarding checklist that reduces time-to-first-success for enterprise customers to 4 weeks or less.
- Define a clear, timebound escalation matrix and triage playbook for Sev 1/2 incidents.
- Standardize integration requirements and delivery expectations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Provide health-check metrics and a QBR agenda template to align with customer success outcomes.

Owners and Roles
- Document owner: Customer Success (Asha Banerjee)
- Primary teams: customer-success, eng-platform, eng-infra, eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, security-and-compliance
- Escalation contacts: Support L1 (shared mailbox + Slack #support-queue), Support L2 (on-call rotation), SRE/Platform (page policy), Solutions Engineering (assigned SE)

1) Enterprise Onboarding Checklist (Phases and Deliverables)
Phase 0: Contract and Security Review (pre-kickoff)
1. Verify signed contract and scope of work, including Dedicated/Private clauses, data residency, and compliance requirements.
2. Exchange legal and security contacts; complete initial NDA and SOC2/ISO evidence exchange if required.
3. Provision access: create org in Redwood Console, invite customer admin(s), issue API keys scoped to a sandbox project.

Phase 1: Kickoff (Week 0) - Stakeholders and Goals
- Deliverables: Kickoff slide deck, success metrics, project timeline (RACI), initial risk register.
- Attendees: Customer exec sponsor, Engineering lead, Security contact, CS lead, SE.
- Agenda (30-60 minutes): introductions, product overview, success metrics, high-level timeline, immediate blockers.

Phase 2: Integration and Validation (Weeks 1-3)
- Integration checklist:
  - Network & Connectivity: validate outbound connectivity to api.redwood.ai (hosted) or private endpoints, confirm whitelisting requirements and firewall rules.
  - Auth & Keys: verify API key rotation policy, KMS integration for Private deployments, and least-privilege roles.
  - Dataset onboarding: sample prompt set, safety and PII review, prompt templates.
  - Performance testing: run guided load test 95th percentile latency target verification, token throughput baseline.
  - Monitoring: connect customer logs and metrics to Console + optional Datadog/Splunk exporters.
- Acceptance criteria: end-to-end generation call succeeds, baseline latency < configured SLO for small-scale tests, telemetry visible in Console.

Phase 3: Pilot and Ramp (Weeks 3-8)
- Execute pilot with limited production traffic and monitoring.
- Validate error budgets, auto-scaling behavior, and cost estimates.
- Agree on rollout plan and canary percentage for traffic.

Phase 4: Production Handoff and QBR Cadence
- Handoff doc: runbook, ownership matrix, alert thresholds, escalation contacts, scheduled maintenance windows.
- Set QBR cadence (monthly for first 3 months, then quarterly).

2) Escalation Playbook
Purpose: respond to high-severity incidents with a predictable triage and communication pattern.
Severity definitions:
- Sev 1 (Customer production outage): API returning >= 50% 5xx or end-user outage for > 5 minutes for a single enterprise customer.
- Sev 2 (Major degradation): Latency or error increase impacting customer SLAs but with partial functionality.
- Sev 3 (Minor): Functional bug or UX issue with low customer impact.

Escalation matrix and SLA targets:
- L1 Support triage: acknowledge within 15 minutes; initial diagnosis within 30 minutes.
- L2 / Engineering on-call: engaged within 30-60 minutes depending on severity.
- Exec and customer success notifications: initial status update within 60 minutes for Sev1, 4 hours for Sev2.

Escalation steps (Sev1)
1. Triage in Support queue: gather request id, timestamps, sample payload, customer region, and environment (hosted/dedicated/private).
2. Execute basic checks: service status page, recent deploys, known-issues list, quota/billing checks, cluster capacity.
3. Page SRE on-call and assigned SE. Use structured subject: '[SEV1] <customer-name> <short-symptom>'.
4. Maintain a single Slack channel for the incident; CS rep should post customer-facing updates every 30 minutes.
5. Postmortem: within 72 hours produce incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation, and action items.

Communication templates
- Initial acknowledgement (example):
  Hi <Customer-Contact>,
  We have received your report and are investigating. Initial details: <summary>. We will provide an update within 60 minutes.

Support Team

- Escalation page subject example:
  [SEV1] AcmeCorp generation 5xx errors - region us-west-2

3) Integration Guide (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
Network and firewall rules (example)
- Hosted: allow outbound TLS 443 to api.redwood.ai and telemetry endpoints. Example CIDR ranges: 52.44.0.0/16, 34.120.0.0/14 (customer-specific ranges provided in onboarding portal).
- Dedicated/Private: follow provided RFC1918 mapping and VPN/BGP peering instructions; if using private endpoints supply customer FQDN and cert chain to security team.

Auth and secrets
- Supported auth modes: API key (short-lived recommended), OAuth for console access, KMS-backed encryption for dedicated/private.
- Rotation: recommend 30-day key rotation for sandbox, 90-day for production; document changes in the customer runbook.

Performance tuning checklist
- Model selection: select model variant based on latency/cost tradeoff; default is redwood-llama-13b-rt for interactive workloads.
- Batching: enable auto-batching for high QPS workloads, target batch size 8-16 depending on latency SLOs.
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Sample curl smoke test
- Hosted:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-13b-rt","input":"hello"}'

4) Known Issues and Workarounds (Living table)
- Issue: intermittent 5xx errors during autoscaler events
  Workaround: temporarily pin routing to Dedicated pool or increase pre-warmed nodes; ensure K8s pod disruption budget is set to at least 1 for critical pools.
- Issue: slow cold-start for large quantized models on new nodes
  Workaround: enable kernel preloading or keep a small pool of warm nodes; use lightweight model variants for low-latency tiers.
- Issue: prompt injection / privacy concerns detected in user prompts
  Workaround: apply input filtering rules and sensitive token masking; route high-risk prompts to restricted model variants or human review.

5) Health Check & QBR Materials
Standard health-check metrics (collect last 30/90 days)
- Availability: API success rate (goal >= 99.95%)
- Latency: 95th and 99th percentile per-route latency vs SLO
- Cost: tokens per transaction and monthly cost trend vs budget
- Error budget burn: percentage used and projected depletion date
- Throughput: peak QPS and typical concurrency
- Model quality: sampled evals for prompt set, regression alerts count

QBR agenda template (60 minutes)
1. Executive summary (5 minutes): health, top wins, top risks
2. Usage and adoption (10 minutes): adoption trends, notable apps/teams, cost per unit analysis
3. Reliability and performance (10 minutes): SLOs, incidents since last QBR, remediation status
4. Roadmap and features (15 minutes): upcoming product changes that impact customer (e.g., Dedicated upgrades, new quantization profiles)
5. Action items and next steps (10 minutes): prioritized list, owners, deadlines
6. Open discussion (10 minutes)

6) Runbooks and Operational Playbooks (Quick reference)
- Restarting a model pool (Dedicated):
  1. Verify affected pool in Console.
  2. Put pool into maintenance mode.
  3. Scale down incrementally and then scale up with new image.
  4. Monitor 95th percentile latency and error rate for 30 minutes before removing maintenance mode.

- Rolling back a deployment (Hosted):
  1. Identify last known-good commit and image.
  2. Trigger rollback via deployment UI or CLI.
  3. Notify CS and impacted customers.
  4. Monitor for degraded performance for 60 minutes.

Operational thresholds (example)
- Alert: error rate > 1% sustained for 10 minutes for enterprise routes -> page Support L2 and SRE.
- Alert: 99th pctl latency > configured SLO + 200ms for 5 minutes -> create incident and notify SE.

7) Postmortem and RCA expectations
- Postmortem template: timeline, impact, root cause, mitigation, long-term fix, owners, ETA.
- Timebox: initial internal RCA draft within 72 hours, final postmortem published within 7 days.

8) Metrics and Reporting (data sources)
- Primary sources: Redwood Console metrics, customer telemetry (if connected), SLO dashboards in Grafana, incident timeline in PagerDuty.
- Export examples: JSON payloads for token usage and latency can be pulled via the Console API endpoint /v1/metrics/export.

Appendices
A. Example onboarding timeline (2-month plan)
- Week 0: Contract sign, kickoff
- Week 1: Network, auth, sample calls
- Week 2: Performance tests, initial telemetry
- Week 3-4: Pilot traffic, tuning
- Week 5-8: Gradual ramp, handoff and QBR scheduling

B. Contacts and escalation directory
- Support: support@redwood.ai, Slack #support-queue
- On-call SRE: see PagerDuty rota (linked in Console)
- Customer Success: asha.banerjee@redwood.ai
- Sales and Legal contacts: available on the contract cover sheet

C. Change log
- 2026-12-15: Published initial comprehensive playbook (Asha Banerjee).
- 2026-12-31: Updated escalation SLAs and added known-issues entry for kernel preloading (reviewers Marco Alvarez, Priya Natarajan).

If you are executing onboarding or an escalation using this playbook and you find a missing step or outdated contact, open a PR against this doc and add the label 'onboarding-updates'. For restricted or customer-sensitive details (certs, PSAs), see the associated restricted runbooks in security-and-compliance.
